title: Sparse active causal intervention programming of unknown finite operations

parent.qualification: WSP56 focused+G29 pass, inherited full regression pending

question: Can a source-blind, zero-gradient solver infer unobserved operator responses with fewer than 28 complete unary examples, and does choosing informative physical interventions outperform random interventions under an equal action budget?
hypothesis: A table-candidate elimination mechanism with causal composition constraints and interventions ranked by predicted output diversity will give >10 percentage-point exact coverage gain over a seeded random-query control on their shared unseen query set, without wrong-confident predictions.

source.code: new standalone evaluator-only WSP57/source.py; no WSP56/WSP53 generator import
source.cohort: SELFTEST only; six frozen independent seeds 2301 through 2306; DEV/PRIMARY forbidden
source.world: 4 hidden distinct random non-affine permutations on seven physical states, sampled by deterministic seed with no fixed semantics passed to learner
source.intervention: query (first-operator-channel, second-operator-channel, before-state) -> observed final state; channels are primitive actions, not language tokens
source.common_training: Exactly 3 unary input->output probes for each of four operators at states 0,2,4 (12 charged actions) supplied identically to both arms
source.action_budget: 24 additional charged two-operator physical queries per arm, selected sequentially without observing outcomes ahead of selection
source.arms: active maximizes current finite-hypothesis output diversity; seeded-random chooses uniformly among unqueried actions; both receive equal 36 total charged interactions
source.eval: all ordered distinct operator pairs and seven before-states (84 candidates), excluding every pair query charged by either arm; same remaining heldout set for both arms
source.isolation: private permutation tables and heldout outputs never provided to learner. Outcomes for chosen charged actions are evaluator-supplied only after selection.

learner.prior: Each operator is a permutation on seven states, not prewired lookup/true family or affine arithmetic; numeric state and four primitive action channels declared
learner.mechanism: Enumerate at most 24 admissible completions per operator after 3 unary probes; arc-consistency filtering from observed compositions; predict only unanimous candidates; no gradients
learner.state: persist public action history, surviving candidate function tables and schema-hashed cold snapshot; no hidden source import

metrics: Active versus random exact predictions and abstentions on identically unseen common queries (micro and per-seed)
Number of consistent table completions after initial unary and final pairs
Seeded action trajectory receipts and strict action-cost parity
Cold-restored prediction parity and canonical/tamper failures
Comparison against unary-only observational baseline (same 12 unary actions, fewer physical queries explicitly not action matched)
criterion: SELFTEST_SIGNAL only if active-minus-random accuracy on common heldouts >=0.10 absolute, active exact coverage >=0.40, zero wrong-confident across both arms, all 6 worlds complete with 36 charged actions/arm and cold restore valid. Else preserve negative/inconclusive without retuning.
stop_rules: No tuning after withheld results; no reusing WSP56 observed worlds or hidden operation maps
No oracle truth tables in learner or active selector; source evaluator may only reveal outcomes of charged chosen actions
Ambiguity -> abstain, no random confident guesses
No protected first-use, merge, deployment, official research-loop integration or paid APIs/scheduled tasks

A positive result only indicates selective intervention value in a small finite permutation world; full conventional, independent symbolic and external-distribution controls required before scientific claims
